audit_findings.title: Unpaid VACCO sale tax may be missing from the cash bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 bridge adjustment; the filed $59 million tax was paid before the reported $73.236 million June 2026 cash balance
audit_findings.mechanism: Would reduce bridge cash if unpaid, but the June cash balance already reflects payment
audit_findings.evidence: The Company anticipates a tax payment of approximately $59 million to be paid during fiscal 2026 related to the gain on sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q resolves the possibility: approximately $59 million was paid during the second quarter, discontinued-operations operating cash flow was negative $59.340 million, and current income tax payable fell from $62.007 million to $5.754 million. Therefore, the June cash bridge does not omit this claim.
audit_findings.action: Document the 10-Q payment reconciliation; no valuation rerun is needed unless evidence identifies a separate remaining VACCO tax liability.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized-software spending may have been stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.844 million in 2025 and $11.903 million in 2024; the 2025 amount is 11.1% of the $143.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted maintenance software investment would overstate annual owner earnings and potentially the historical growth trend
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company incurred expenditures for capitalized software and other of $15.8 million in 2025 and $11.9 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash expenditure is demonstrated, but its omission from the OE worksheet is unresolved. Even if the entire 2025 amount were missing, the exposure is 11.1% of the anchor and would only lower values already capped at $104.35 per share versus the $274.02 market price; it cannot reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE observation to operating cash flow and separately deduct maintenance capitalized-software additions, while avoiding a second deduction for their amortization.

audit_findings.title: The signed Megger acquisition has no funding or dilution scenario
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $2.35 billion consideration, comprising $0.9 billion cash and approximately $1.4 billion of ESCO equity; actual issued-share count unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adds Megger owner earnings and growth but also changes shares, debt, interest expense, fees, assumed liabilities, and bridge cash
audit_findings.evidence: We also continue to seek opportunities to supplement our growth by making strategic acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a signed but unclosed transaction and therefore is not presently part of the filed operating perimeter. The latest filing supplies material consideration and financing terms, contradicting the premise that funding information is unavailable, but it still does not establish post-close owner earnings or the actual share count. The transaction is large enough to make the standalone valuation unsuitable as a post-close valuation.
audit_findings.action: At closing, replace the standalone case with a post-transaction rerun using actual shares issued, debt drawn, cash used, fees, assumed liabilities, purchase accounting, interest, and normalized Megger owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: The historical trend may include earnings from disposed VACCO
audit_findings.mechanism: Contaminated historical OE would alter the log-trend anchor; sale proceeds or residual cash could also create perimeter inconsistency through the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: VACCO is reflected as discontinued operations in the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes for all periods shown in this Annual Report.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing demonstrates that only its presented periods were recast for discontinued operations. It does not establish whether the 2016-2022 OE observations were rebuilt. VACCO reported both profits and a loss in the available periods, so the direction and size of any older-period contamination cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2022 OE from continuing operations, removing VACCO earnings, depreciation, capital spending, working capital, disposal effects, and related financing or taxes; then recompute the log-trend anchor.

audit_findings.title: Growth may rely on acquisition capital that the forecast does not charge
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-supported historical growth can inflate the 6%-8% forecast without deducting the cash needed for future acquisitions
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities from continuing operations was $524.2 million in 2025 and $96.6 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate substantial acquisition spending, including $472.006 million in 2025, $56.383 million in 2024, and $17.694 million in 2023. They also show growth outside Maritime, but do not isolate organic owner-earnings growth or establish whether 6%-8% can be sustained without further purchased businesses. The potential forecast overstatement is therefore unresolved and cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Calculate constant-perimeter organic revenue, EBIT, and OE growth excluding Maritime, MPE, CMT, and other acquisitions; rerun growth scenarios if organic evidence does not support 6%-8%.

audit_findings.title: The operating numerator is stale and contains only a partial year of Maritime
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed trailing-four-quarter continuing net earnings through June 2026 are $139.836 million, $23.537 million or 20.2% above fiscal 2025; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A current TTM rebuild would change the OE anchor by adding subsequent Maritime and legacy earnings while retaining related interest, taxes, working capital, reinvestment, SBC, and other costs
audit_findings.evidence: Maritime contributed $95.2 million in revenue in 2025 since the date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch and partial-year Maritime inclusion are demonstrated. Filed TTM continuing earnings indicate a potentially meaningful numerator increase, but net earnings are not owner earnings and the record does not establish the combined effect of higher amortization, financing costs, working capital, and reinvestment. Materiality to the DCF therefore remains uncertain rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild trailing-four-quarter OE through June 2026 from the quarterly cash-flow and operating statements, including full Maritime operations and all related interest, taxes, SBC, working capital, PP&E spending, and capitalized software; then recompute the trend anchor and scenarios.
